note: Field names, stat keys and union values follow src/domain. Percentages are decimals. Descriptions stay verbatim. Every mechanic is also carried as values: a grant names its recipient and its stats, params carry the numbers a condition needs, and combat says whether the entry changes anything inside a fight.

sources.lolchess.gg: units and their abilities; the Set 18 wisp and augment pools, with gold, tier, category and appearance condition
sources.metatft.com: trait descriptions, augment stages and the augment category taxonomy
sources.communitydragon.org: Riot data, PBE snapshot dated 2026-07-31. Trait names and breakpoints, wisp identifiers and variables, timeless item stats, and the 29 augments this set brought of its own
sources.tactics.tools: an earlier build — it still says Eldritch, Sunbeam and Moonbeam. Read to date the other sources, never to value them

set-18/units.json.verified: 65 units, 14/13/14/14/10 by cost, plus six summoned entities. Traits agree with traits.json in both directions. Kobuko and Alune match Community Dragon on every stat. Every ability carries the numbers its tooltip states outside the breakdown. Four stars are a 1-, 2- and 3-cost affair: all 41 of them carry a fourth value, none of the 4- and 5-costs does

set-18/traits.json.verified: 36 names against Community Dragon, no divergence either way, and 34 of the 36 breakpoint ladders identical. Rosters cover the 65 units. Every breakpoint carries its grants and its parameters, read from the tooltip

set-18/wisps.json.verified: The client defines 181 charms; the published sources carried 163 of them, and gold, category and description agree on those. 84 change a fight and are decomposed into grants. The 14 the aggregators omit are economy — gold, experience, player health, streaks — and were added from the client on 2026-08-14 with their name, their cost and their values. Six of them get their description back by matching the curve rows the client's own text quotes; the other eight quote a row name too common to tell one charm from another, and stay null along with every category and appearance window. Crystal Ball was dropped: neither its name nor its text appears anywhere in the 14262 strings the client ships

timeless/augments.json.verified: 255 distinct augments across 257 rows: Beast Within and Beast Within+ each appear twice, same tier and same apparition, differing only in the champion they hand out — Sivir or Nidalee. lolchess and metatft agree on every name and every tier. 240 matched to Riot Set 18 entries; 99 carry combat effects and are decomposed into grants

timeless/items.json.verified: 137 items: 10 components, 39 craftables, 20 emblems, 32 artifacts, 36 radiants. The eight-by-eight grid is closed. Seven stat lines corrected against Community Dragon

timeless/roles.json.verified: Six archetypes read from CT_Role_Stats in the shipped client on 2026-08-14. No published source carries them. The fighter attack-speed series keeps the client keys 1, 3, 4, 5 and 10; what that axis counts is not established

keywords.json.verified: Read on 2026-08-15 from Game_locchunk1.locres in the shipped client — 17909 keys, 14248 strings. Eight names carry the client's own definition verbatim, taken from the <rules> block it wraps them in; Bleed carries ours. Four stacking rules stay null: the client states one for Shred, Sunder and Burn only

more.adaptor: Their main stats (AP or AD) can vary, therefor, scaling key accept only an array as value.
more.keyword: The nine named effects a catalog entry can apply: Burn, Wound, Shred, Sunder, Slow, Vulnerable, Precision, Mana Reave and Bleed. keywords.json holds each one once — what it does, which way it points, how it stacks, and the shape it takes in the modifier vocabulary. It carries no magnitude, because a magnitude belongs to whatever applies it: Inferno burns for 1% at two breakpoints and 3% at seven, Red Buff for 1%, a charm for 2.5% once prismatic. Eight definitions are the client's own words; Bleed is ours, because the client applies it and never defines it. Chill was dropped — the client renders its ChillAmount row as a percentage of Slow and never shows the word.
more.applies: What an entry applies to whoever it lands on, named rather than described. Each item names a keyword and carries its magnitude; a null magnitude is one the game applies without writing the number, and it waits on a curve table. A magnitude is flat or a share depending on what the source states — Shred is 30% on Void Staff and a flat 10 on Fiddlesticks, which is why the keyword itself carries no unit. The duration sits on the item when it is its own, on the grant when several keywords share it, and an item recurring inside that duration says so with everySeconds. A grant that only modifies stats has no applies, and a keyword never lands in stats or percentStats.
more.namesTheKeyword: Where a keyword lands is decided on evidence, never on resemblance. The game naming it in the entry's own text is the first proof; Riot naming it in the data behind that text is the second, and it is what turns Counterspell into Mana Reave — the tooltip spells the definition out without the word — and a flat resistance loss into Shred, whose curve row Riot calls MagicResistShred. Resemblance on its own proves nothing, and it usually turns out to be shallow: of the five entries that take a share of max health as damage, one alone matches the whole of Burn, and nothing in the game calls it Burn either. Elder Dragon's Ignite and Draven's bleed deal physical damage where the keyword they resemble deals true, and Lightning Strike lands once where a Burn ticks.
more.id: Kebab-case slug, the casing the rest of the vocabulary uses, because the engine reads an id as a Record key and nothing else. Set content is prefixed by its set — s18-adaptor, s18-akali — so a Set 19 trait of the same name lands beside it rather than on top of it; timeless content is not. Apostrophes and punctuation drop, a trailing + becomes -plus, roman numerals stay: rek-sai, thiefs-gloves, celestial-blessing-i, champ-delivery-plus. Two augments share a name and differ by the champion they hand out, so their slug carries it: beast-within-sivir, beast-within-nidalee.
more.iconPath: One versioned file per entry, taken from the client. wisps.json carries none — a wisp is text. Lux is one entry with ten variants and a single icon: the client ships no art that tells them apart, so the interface will need a treatment of its own to show which one is in play. Ghoul and Kruglette carry none either — they come out of Yorick's and Krug's spells and never appear in a catalogue.
more.role: Riot names a role on two axes rather than one: an archetype — tank, brawler, fighter, assassin, marksman, caster — and a damage type, attack, magic or hybrid. Our role field carries the archetype and damageProfile the second axis, where an array of two is Riot's hybrid. timeless/roles.json holds what an archetype does on its own.
more.summoned: A summoned entity comes out of a trait or a spell and is never placed, so it belongs in no catalogue the player picks from. That is what summoned marks, and it is the only field that does: combat is true on all sixty-five units and cost is merely absent here. targetable used to sit on three of the six and was dropped — being in this file is what makes a unit targetable, and whether it shows in an interface is not a combat question.
more.sacrificeRole: Which bucket a sacrificed unit falls into for Blackthorn. The client keeps three — tank, attack, magic — and reads the first off the archetype, the other two off the damage profile. A hybrid profile fits none of them, and the client's fourth effect, NoRole, carries no values at all. One unit lands there: Master Yi. He is filed as attack, and the reason is his resource rather than his kit — the magic bucket spends half its value on mana regeneration, which an ammo unit has no bar for, while the attack bucket gives attack speed, which fills ammo faster. Reasoned, not read: the effect that assigns the bucket is one this extraction cannot open.
more.resource: What a unit's bar counts before it casts. Most count mana. Caitlyn and Master Yi count attacks, Kayle counts nothing and casts on another rule, Gnar fills with rage on a timer as well as on attacks. The client keeps a fourth kind, time, and no unit here has been tied to it.
more.combat: True when the engine can read the entry and produce an exact number from it. The Coven trait is false: holding it grants no combat bonus, only essence. The Coven Acolyte augment is true. Composition effects are false — Apex Predator takes team slots, Avatar counts double towards breakpoints, neither lands inside a fight.
more.requiresRunInput: True when the entry carries a state no calculation derives and no player can reproduce on demand: a choice taken during a run, or a counter carried across rounds. The user declares it before the fight, and the data enumerates the options without designating one. What each entry expects is written beside it here.
more.team: A grant to team excludes the trait holders. Juggernaut at six gives its Juggernauts 34% durability and everyone else 8% — never the sum.
more.prose: The catalog files carry data and nothing else. A remark, a caveat, an observation — anything a reader needs and a parser does not — lives here instead, keyed by what it explains. Nine note fields were lifted out of traits.json and units.json on 2026-08-11; what follows is what they said.
more.summonScaling: A summoned entity scales off the trait that brought it, through the formula its scaling field states. Two rules the formula does not show: a duplicated champion counts once towards the trait's star total, and flat team bonuses land after the scaling rather than before. Elderwood plants take a third factor the trait never mentions — the stage multiplies their health on a curve of its own, one per plant, so the same board reads differently at stage two and at stage six.
more.null: A field set to null is a question the extraction asked and could not answer, told apart from a field that is absent because the entry has no use for it. Fourteen wisps carry three of them — category, description and appears — because the client keeps those on an object whose property names a shipped build strips out.
more.consumables: The nine Doodad, Knick-Knack and Thingamajig wisps hand out consumables rather than stats. consumableOptions lists what a single one can grant and designates none, because the game rolls it: Doodad gives armour and magic resist or health, Knick-Knack attack damage or attack speed, Thingamajig ability power or mana regeneration. The grants are permanent and the consumable is spent on use.
more.upgraded: A wisp has three states: taken, upgraded, and prismatic. Blossom upgrades every wisp from three onwards, so the upgraded value is not an edge case. Where the client gives both, the second lands beside the first under the same name with an Upgraded suffix. The client spells the same idea four ways — UpgradeCost, CostUpgrade, Cost_Upgrade, Upgrade_Cost — and all four are read as costUpgraded here. A handful of pairs do not share a stem, because the base value was named from a tooltip and the upgraded one from the client: Nature's Ally carries allyDeathsPerSummon beside championDeathsPerSummonUpgraded. The prismatic state reads the same way, with a Prismatic suffix, and only twenty-one wisps have one — Blossom names it at eleven, where its tooltip says wisps overflow with power, and the client keeps the list in that trait's own folder. It is a different regime rather than another notch: Truce pays one gold taken, two upgraded, and a hundred prismatic.
more.byStar: A plant's series is indexed by its own star level, not by the tier of the trait that summoned it. Elderwood sets that star level itself: one up to seven, two at nine, three at eleven. Series that stop before three do so because the client's curve repeats its last value, not because a value is missing.
more.covenEssence: The Coven trait is economy on its own. Dark Ritual and Coven Acolyte are what turn its essence into combat power.
more.blackthorn: traitBonusMultiplier amplifies the sacrifice table alone; the team health grant is flat per breakpoint. It grows with the breakpoint rather than repeating — 1 at two, 1.25 at four, 1.5 at six.
more.description: Written for a tooltip, not for a paragraph. Sections are separated by a blank line — passive, active, per-breakpoint scale, and any keyword it leans on. Inside a section, a line break every proposition, so no line runs long enough to wrap. Numbers are references into breakdown rather than literals: the engine recomputes them against the stats of the moment, and a figure frozen at one star with no items is wrong as soon as anything modifies it.
